subject: web-technology-1
name: Web Technology I
exam: TU assessment: 60% final examination set by the university, 40% internal (assignments, lab work, attendance).

units.title: Internet and the World Wide Web
topics: Web server, browser, search engine and hosting
Seeing the Web: machines, messages and addresses

sections.title: Web server, browser, search engine and hosting
Seeing the Web: machines, messages and addresses

summary: The Web is a service on the Internet built from URLs, HTTP and HTML; clients request and servers respond.
DNS turns names into IP addresses; HTTP is stateless and uses methods and status codes; cookies carry sessions.
Browsers render; servers serve static or dynamic content; mail uses SMTP, POP3 and IMAP.

units.title: HTML and Graphics
topics: Graphics: images, image maps, canvas and SVG
Seeing HTML: browsers, trees and boxes

sections.title: Graphics: images, image maps, canvas and SVG
Seeing HTML: browsers, trees and boxes

summary: HTML structures content with nested elements; the head describes the page and the body shows it.
Text, links, images, lists and tables carry content; forms collect input with typed, validated controls.
Semantic elements give meaning; video, audio and iframe embed media; SVG and canvas draw graphics.

units.title: Scripting Language (JavaScript)
topics: Arrays, objects, strings, Math, Date, JSON
Seeing JavaScript: people, scope, events and the loop

sections.title: Arrays, objects, strings, Math, Date, JSON
Seeing JavaScript: people, scope, events and the loop

summary: JavaScript adds behaviour: variables and types, control flow, functions and closures, arrays, objects and JSON.
The DOM and events let scripts read and change the page; forms are validated before submission.
Errors use try/catch/finally; timers and promises handle work that finishes later.

units.title: CSS (Cascading Style Sheets)
topics: Syntax and ways to add CSS
Seeing CSS: the box, the cascade and the layout

sections.title: Syntax and ways to add CSS
Seeing CSS: the box, the cascade and the layout

summary: CSS styles HTML through selectors; the cascade resolves conflicts by importance, specificity and order.
The box model determines element size and spacing; units can be absolute or relative.
display, position, Flexbox and Grid build layouts; transitions and media queries add polish and responsiveness.

units.title: XML (Extensible Markup Language)
topics: Seeing XML: trees, errors, validation and size

sections.title: Seeing XML: trees, errors, validation and size

summary: XML describes data with custom tags under strict well-formedness rules.
DTDs and XML Schemas make a document valid against a grammar; namespaces avoid name clashes.
CSS and XSLT present XML; DOM and SAX parse it; JSON has taken over most web-API use.

units.title: Introduction to jQuery
topics: Getting and setting content, attributes, CSS, classes
Seeing jQuery: selection, chaining, effects and traversal

sections.title: Getting and setting content, attributes, CSS, classes
Seeing jQuery: selection, chaining, effects and traversal

summary: jQuery selects elements with CSS selectors and applies short methods to all matches.
It reads and writes content, attributes and styles, builds and removes DOM nodes, and handles events (including delegated ones).
Effects and chaining make UI code compact; AJAX helpers load data without a page reload.

units.title: Website Page Layout and Design Issues
topics: Seeing design issues: access, contrast, weight and structure

sections.title: Seeing design issues: access, contrast, weight and structure

summary: Good sites start with purpose, audience, site map and wireframes.
Layout, navigation, typography and colour must support reading and finding things; contrast can be measured.
Accessibility, performance, SEO and compatibility are design requirements, not extras.
Security basics and a final checklist precede publishing.
